_meanings:
.²1 Direct perception or cognition, knowledge derived from personal observation
 or experiment, notion, apprehension, the impression on the mind not derived
 from memory, one of the kinds of knowledge; {#sarvavyavahAraheturjYAnaM#}
 {#budDiH . sA dviviDA ssftiranuBavaSca . saMskAramAtrajanyaM jYAnaM smftiH .#}
 {#tadBinnaM jYAnamanuBavaH#} which again is {#yaTArTa#} right & {#ayaTArTa#}
 wrong. See <ls>T. S. 34</ls>. (The Naiyāyikas recognize {#pratyakza, anumAna#},
 {#upamAna#} and {#SAbda#} as the four sources of knowledge; the Vedāntins
 and Mīmāṃsakas

 add two more {#arTApatti#} and {#anupalabDi#}; the Vaiśeṣikas and Bauddhas
 admit the first two only, the Sāṅkhyas exclude {#upamAna#}, while the
 Chārvākas admit {#pratyakza#} only. Other sections of philosophical
 schools add three more to the six sources of knowledge recognised by the
 Mīmāṃsakas:-- {#saMBava#} ‘equivalence’; {#Etihya#} ‘fallible testimony’,
 and {#cezwA#} ‘gesture’.)
.²2 Experience; {#anuBavaM vacasA saKi lumpasi#} <ls>N. 4. 105</ls>.
.²3 Understanding.
.²4 Result, consequence.
